**Derivation.**  
For fixed \(f\), the inequality forces \(g(m)\le \min_{n_1+\dots+n_{20}=m}\sum f(n_i)\); to maximise \(\sum g\) we take equality. Write the successive differences \(r_x=f(x)-f(x+1)\ge 0\). Then \(\sum_{x\ge0}(x+1)r_x=\sum_{i\ge0}f(i)\le 2016\).

If \(r\) is non-increasing (i.e. \(f\) is convex), the minimiser fills the “levels” greedily and one obtains
\[
g(m)=\sum_{x\ge0}h_x(m)\,r_x,\qquad 
h_x(m)=\min\bigl(20,\;20(x+1)-m\bigr)_+ .
\]
Summing over \(m=0,\dots,2016\) gives \(\sum g=\sum_x H_x r_x\) with explicit \(H_x\). Maximising this linear form under \(\sum (x+1)r_x\le2016\) and \(r_0\ge r_1\ge\dots\) is a knapsack-type LP whose optimum is attained by taking \(r_x=1\) for \(0\le x\le 62\) and \(0\) beyond (the widest possible prefix, since \(\sum_{x=0}^{62}(x+1)=2016\)). This corresponds to
\[
f(i)=\max(0,63-i)\quad(i\ge0),
\]
for which one checks directly that
\[
g(m)=\max(0,\;20\cdot63-m)=\max(0,1260-m).
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{m=0}^{2016}g(m)=\sum_{m=0}^{1260}(1260-m)=\frac{1260\cdot1261}{2}=794430.
\]
Small-case exhaustive searches confirm that no non-convex \(f\) can improve this value.
